newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha steady despite weaker crude oil.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha steady despite weaker crude oil.

text.p: Naphtha prices were little moved in afternoon Tokyo trade on Tuesday despite mild losses on overnight crude oil markets in London and New York, market participants said.
"Although crude prices dropped overnight, there was a big enough number of active players in the market today to support naphtha levels," one dealer said.
Firmer European naphtha was another reason behind stable naphtha prices in Tokyo, traders also said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half September was offered at $210.00 per tonne, while bids were heard at $209.00.
It was traded between western traders at $210.50 in late dealing on Monday, traders said.
The contango in near-term naphtha spreads broadened slightly, with second-half September/second-half October discussed at minus 75 cents/even. It was quoted at minus 50 cents/even on Monday.

Japan's domestic naphtha output in June grew 21.8 percent from a year earlier to 1.18 million kilolitres, reflecting healthy demand from the petrochemical sector, while naphtha imports dipped by 1.4 percent over the same period, the trade ministry said on Tuesday. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
